newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen plays down analyst briefing note.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen plays down analyst briefing note.

text.p: PowerGen Plc on Monday played down a Financial Times report that it had written to analysts alerting them to expect profits at the low end of the range of previous forecasts.
A spokesman for the electricity generator said the letter was a briefing note, sent late last month, which did no more than summarise information of which they should have been already aware.
"The note included for their information a range of key analyst forecasts but made very clear they were the forecasts of analysts and not those of the company," the spokesman said.
The FT said the range quoted by the company was between 530 million stg and 585 million, which compares with a range between 520 million stg to 668 million cited by the Estimate Directory.
However, that Esimate Directory range could have excluded a one-off charge of some 70 million stg the company will take this year over its deal to buy out its partner in Kinetica, Conoco (UK) Ltd.
Announding the Kinetica buy on March 20, PowerGen had said it would take a charge of not more than 69 million stg to cover the company's gas purchase contracts.
The PowerGen spokesman also pointed out that the range of dividend expectations cited in the letter was between 24.2p and 27.1p, not between 27.1p and 34.2p as the FT had said.

Analysts said the letter was in effect designed to take the place of the usual briefing for industry watchers, frequently held by companies before they go into a "closed season" in the run-up to results.
"They took the view that there was no need for a pre-closed season meeting as there was little of the company's performance analysts should not already be aware," said one.
By 1028 GMT, the stock had recovered from an early tumble to be unchanged at 616p, after initially dropping 11-1/4p in the wake of the FT report.
PowerGen is due to report full-year results on May 22.
